key_insight: UniD shows that a single video model can learn to predict many dense scene properties at once even when the training data is split across separate, incompatible datasets. This reduces the need for fully labeled multi-task datasets or expensive pseudo-label generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the fragmentation of dense prediction annotations across different datasets and domains. Existing unified models either require fully co-annotated data, which is scarce, or costly pseudo-labeling, which is inefficient at scale.
method: Introduces UniD, a unified video model for jointly predicting eight dense scene properties from video.
Trains on disjoint datasets rather than relying only on fully annotated multi-task samples.
Leverages video-based learning to connect geometry, appearance, and semantic understanding across tasks.
impact: This approach makes multi-task dense prediction more practical and scalable for real-world AI systems. For practitioners, it lowers the annotation burden while enabling richer scene understanding from diverse datasets.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing disjoint datasets feeding into one unified video model
A task wheel or matrix illustrating the eight dense prediction outputs
A comparison chart of fully co-annotated training vs. disjoint-data training vs. pseudo-labeling
Icons representing depth, normals, semantics, and other scene properties
paper_title: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data
paper_authors: Yihong Sun, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Bharath Hariharan, Joon-Young Lee
